description:
Your food is incredible. Your events run like clockwork. So why aren’t you booked out?

On Booked & Plated, chef turned web designer Amy Ogden helps independent caterers see that getting booked isn't a ‘you’ problem, it's a ‘systems’ problem.

After 25 years in the culinary field, Amy knows you already trust systems with everything from prep lists to pre-event checks. Your website should work the same way. A pretty site isn't enough. You need something sustainable that's constantly working in the background to keep new clients coming in.

In quick 3 to 5 minute episodes every Monday and Tuesday, Amy breaks down the barriers that might be costing you clients, the bad advice keeping you stuck, and what the most-booked caterers have working behind the scenes.

No jargon, no lectures, just back of the house talk with someone who has been on both sides of the pass and both sides of the screen. The rush is over, flip over a milk crate and let's chat; or book a tour at bookedandplated.com to learn how this done-for-you website system goes live one week from your build date.

title: I Have Never Tasted a Tomato
author: Holger Nauheimer
description:
What happens when artificial intelligence enters the kitchen?
AI knows millions of recipes, but it has never tasted a tomato. And yet, it might change the way we cook.
Can a machine that has never smelled fresh basil, tasted a perfectly ripe peach, or burned its fingers on a hot pan help us become more creative cooks? Can AI invent genuinely new dishes, or does it simply rearrange what humans have already discovered? And what happens to culinary traditions, intuition, and the pleasure of cooking when artificial intelligence becomes part of the creative process?
I Have Never Tasted a Tomato explores these questions through conversations with chefs, food writers, researchers, sensory scientists, and people who are experimenting with AI in real kitchens.
Hosted by Holger Nauheimer, the podcast moves between the science of flavour, the art of cooking, and the deeply personal experiences that shape our relationship with food. Childhood memories, family recipes, spectacular failures, unexpected discoveries, and the dishes we never forget are just as important as algorithms and artificial intelligence.
A podcast about AI and cooking. But above all, about being human.

You know the moment. The engagement numbers come back lower than last year, or your best person hands in their notice, and you realize the old playbook isn't working. Maybe you set the people strategy for the whole company. Maybe you manage a team of six and nobody ever trained you for it. Either way, you're the one people look to when work gets hard.

Success is about more than what we achieve at work. It's about how we grow, lead, learn and live along the way.

So we'll leave you with the same question we ask our guests: What does human success mean to you?

Professions aren't transformed by sweeping mandates or top-down reform decreed by professional bodies. They are remade by bold individuals who dare to reimagine what's possible. As you listen to this book, I encourage you to embrace the challenge. Be the change you seek for your firm and your profession. Because the future of accounting isn't something to observe—it's something to build. Building a Sustainable Accounting Firm illuminates the path forward. title: Buy Ativan at a Cheap Price: Affordable
author: Eva
description:
Finding affordable Ativan starts with comparing legitimate pharmacy prices and understanding available savings options. Ativan (lorazepam) is a prescription medication used to treat certain anxiety conditions. Its price may vary depending on dosage, pharmacy, location, and insurance coverage.Before purchasing, consult your healthcare provider and ask a licensed pharmacist about generic lorazepam, eligible discounts, and other cost-saving options. Compare the total price, including dispensing fees and delivery charges, and ensure the pharmacy is properly licensed and requires a valid prescription.Be cautious of websites advertising unusually cheap Ativan or offering it without a prescription. Unverified medicines may be counterfeit or unsafe. Lorazepam can cause drowsiness, dependence, and serious interactions with alcohol and opioid medications.Choosing a reputable pharmacy and exploring legitimate savings programs can help you manage medication expenses responsibly. Always follow your healthcare professional’s instructions and never change your prescribed dose to save money.Visit here for more info : https://careskit.com/

Welcome to YogaScussion—the premier yoga podcast that goes beyond the mat. Hosted by Gina Clingerman and Brendon Orr, this weekly yoga talk show dives deep into yoga practice, yoga culture, and yoga philosophy with the teachers, healers, writers, and movers who are living it.

This isn't a yoga podcast about perfect poses or performative wellness. It's a conversation about what yoga actually looks like in real life—the injuries, the doubt, the breakthroughs, the joy, and the messy, beautiful middle. We explore how ancient wisdom meets modern life, how a dedicated yoga practice transforms off the mat, and what it means to build community in a world that's forgotten how to connect.

Each episode features honest, in-depth conversations with Gina, Brendon, and guests who bring diverse perspectives—from Ayurvedic physicians and somatic therapists to authors, yoga acharyas, yoga teachers, studio owners, and practitioners. title: The Patching Protocol
author: Alan Patching PhD
description:
Practical, evidence-informed insights into resilience, stress, anxiety and mental health.

The Patching Protocol is an audio podcast designed to help people understand, prevent and manage the effects of stress and anxiety, and to support those experiencing their psychological impacts in finding effective pathways towards recovery.

Drawing on clinical psychotherapy, counselling and hypnotherapy, each episode explores stress and anxiety in an accessible, practical way. The aim is not only to provide useful strategies for managing these experiences, but also to demystify mental health and address some of the concerns and misconceptions that can prevent people from seeking professional help when they need it.

Episodes examine the particular challenges that arise in different circumstances, including preparing for surgery and recovering afterwards, and coping with a troubling medical diagnosis or demanding treatment, such as that associated with cancer.

The podcast also explores two specialist areas of practice. The first is psychological support for women who have experienced repeated IVF failures despite having no identified physical explanation for those outcomes. This work considers the potential role of stress and psychological wellbeing in the IVF experience, and how therapeutic support may help women navigate what can be an emotionally demanding journey.

The second specialist area is workplace mental health, with a particular focus on psychosocial hazards and risks. Drawing on clinical practice, academic research and professional experience, the podcast examines how workplace environments, leadership behaviours, organisational cultures and the way work is managed can affect psychological health. It also considers how individuals and organisations can recognise and address psychosocial hazards, reduce the risks associated with harmful workplace conditions, and create healthier, more psychologically sustainable working environments.

Whether you are seeking to understand your own experiences, support someone close to you, or gain a deeper understanding of the factors affecting mental health at work, The Patching Protocol offers thoughtful, practical insights into the challenges we face and the ways we can respond to them.

Hosted by Dr Alan Patching, PhD, a clinical psychotherapist and hypnotherapist, The Patching Protocol draws on clinical experience, academic research and professional practice to explore the challenges of stress, anxiety and psychological wellbeing, offering evidence-informed perspectives on how we can better manage these challenges in our personal lives and workplaces.

title: GIVE TO GRANT
author: The Community Foundation of Grant County, IN
description:
Give To Grant is a podcast about the people, causes, and projects moving Grant County, Indiana forward, and how they get funded.

Hosted by the Community Foundation of Grant County, the show goes inside the work happening across Marion and the surrounding communities, and introduces you to the people doing it. These are conversations, not lectures. Nobody is being sold to, and the only thing we ever ask for comes in the last thirty seconds.

WHAT YOU'LL HEAR

Behind the Grant goes inside a funded project, told by the people who received the money. What they applied for, what they were up against, and what actually happened after the check cleared.

Fund Spotlight is the donor side of the house. A family who started a fund in someone's memory. A business owner who built one for their employees. A couple who decided to leave something behind. Conversations about why people give, in their own words, without a brochure in sight.

Scholarship Spotlight follows the students. More than 120 scholarship opportunities move through the Foundation every year, and every one of them has a donor on one end and a student on the other. We put them in the same room.

The Build follows the long projects, starting with the Riverfront Canvas public art initiative in downtown Marion. From the first argument about whether murals belong on a riverfront, to the call for artists, to the morning a building-sized piece goes up.

Grant County Voices is wide open. Mayors, nonprofit directors, employers, people who left and came back. Anyone shaping what this county becomes.

On the Table takes on what Grant County is actually talking about. Workforce and why people leave. Housing. Childcare. Recovery and mental health. Food access. Downtown. We name the problem honestly, with real numbers, then spend the rest of the episode with the people already doing something about it.

Easy as Pie is the short explainer. What a community foundation actually is. How endowment works. How to start a fund. What a will does, and why everyone puts it off. Plain English, no jargon.

ABOUT THE COMMUNITY FOUNDATION OF GRANT COUNTY

Since 1984, the Community Foundation of Grant County has been connecting people who care with causes that matter. Every year the Foundation grants more than a million dollars back into this community, supporting the nonprofits, programs, and projects that improve quality of life across Grant County, and offering more than 120 scholarship opportunities to local students through a single universal application.

The Foundation does three things. It builds endowment, so a gift given once keeps giving. It makes local grants, funding the organizations and ideas doing the work on the ground. And it provides community leadership, convening partnerships no single organization could build alone.

The Foundation has a long habit of accentuating the positive, which is not the same as pretending everything is fine. Hard subjects get named plainly here. They just do not get the last word. This podcast is where that work gets told by the people living it.

WHO THIS IS FOR

Donors, and anyone curious about where charitable money actually goes. Nonprofit leaders working in Grant County. Students and families navigating scholarship season. Attorneys, CPAs, and financial advisors whose clients ask about charitable giving. And anyone who lives here and wants good news about this place, with the receipts attached.

LISTEN AND WATCH

New episodes every other week, thirty minutes or less. Available on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and everywhere else you listen. Video episodes on YouTube and Facebook.

GET INVOLVED

Give to an existing fund, start one of your own, apply for a grant or a scholarship, or just see where the money goes. It all starts at givetogrant.org.

— — —

THE EVIDENCE LADDER — how we grade every claim on this show

DOCUMENTED — official record: a FOIA document, hearing testimony, an agency report, an on-record named source.
CORROBORATED — multiple independent witnesses, or a witness plus sensor/recording evidence.
REPORTED — a single source or outlet's claim, named with its date; not independently verified.
LORE — folklore, ancient texts, and in-universe storytelling. Lore is welcome here — it is never silently upgraded.

Every Recent Sightings item runs five prosaic checks on air before any mystery is entertained: aircraft traffic, Starlink trains, balloons, drones, and sensor or lens artifacts. When we get something wrong, we correct it on air in our quarterly Signal Check.

WHO IS SPEAKING? Elowen and Zeth are fictional alien hosts, performed by AI voices under ODIN's editorial oversight. The claims they discuss are real-world claims, graded on the ladder above. In the show, "in our story…" marks lore and in-character memory; "in the record…" marks DOCUMENTED and CORROBORATED material. The hosts may be aliens; the sourcing is not make-believe.

SHARE YOUR SIGHTING — Earth Witness: send your sighting account (location, date, time, duration, what you saw) via our social channels. Every account is graded honestly and read in your own words. Follow the show: Instagram @elowenandzeth · Facebook: Dancing Paintbrush · YouTube: Orlando Dozier channel (Community tab). A production of ODIN.

description:
The Price of Salt – by Claire Morgan & Patricia Highsmith.  
The Price of Salt is a sensitive portrait of blossoming love – between two women. 
It’s easy to see why this book was so explosive when it was first published in 1952, though it seems quite tame reading it now.  
Carol is an affluent married mother of a young daughter who has recently separated from her husband. Therese is a young, would-be set designer who works at a department store to pay the rent on her shabby New York City apartment. Their chance encounter sets both on an expected journey (both psychologically and literally) where they explore the nature of love and must decide how much they are willing to sacrifice to maintain it. Particularly against intense societal pressure, even ostracism.  
The story is told mostly from Therese’s perspective. I deeply valued the wonderful descriptions of what goes through the mind of any person falling in love, regardless of gender. The endless internal monologues, the doubts, the intense sensitivity to reading signals from the partner. And how someone slowly comes to know when something that began as infatuation transitions into something deeper.  
The Price of Salt actually becomes quite a suspenseful read with an end that surprised me, since I began to imagine many different ways the novel might end. A very interesting read.

title: Telling Great Stories
author: Nate S. Campbell
description:
I'm Nate Campbell, and I teach storytelling. This podcast will be your go-to place to learn how to tell great stories because that's the journey I'm on right now. I'm learning to tell great stories. I'm writing my first book with a pen and paper legal notepad, to be specific.

I'll be here every day, sharing with you insights that I've learned, sharing with you the framework that I teach in my book, Telling Great Stories, and sharing with you things that can help you to become a great storyteller and hopefully one day write your own book as well.

So imagine for a second we're going to go up to the top of a mountain on a ski lift together, side by side. When we get up there, we're just going to go up and enjoy the view.


I started on this journey in 2018 through a conversation with my friend Kevin Groves about what I would do if money wasn't a thing. I said I would tell stories of ranchers and farmers because my grandpa Tom now has dementia, and his story'll never be told unless I do it.

It was 8 years ago, and I didn't take action. I started taking action towards this in October, and over the last 3 weeks, I've accomplished more than I have in the prior 8 years.

We need to get off of our ass and do things. We need to get off our ass and take action. We need to get off our ass and tell great stories, because at the end of the day, stories are what matter. Stories are what live beyond our years. Stories are what need to be written down and kept in books.

If you want to work with me, go to www.tellinggreatstories.com and join my waitlist. If you want to read my book, it'll be launching December 13, 2026. You can get it at www.tellinggreatstories.com.

title: The Nonsense of Thomas Rabies
author: Thomas Rabies
description:
Thomas Rabies writes nonsense prose. It is not meant to be printed. It is meant to be heard, as he believes all literature should be. In this ongoing work, a single word can carry two or three meanings at once.


In each episode he reads it out loud, which is what it was made for. Lines echo and bend. A phrase repeats with one letter changed and becomes its own pun. Place names fold in on themselves.


The subjects are small and local on purpose: everyday errands and minor upsets in a northern spa town. Nothing much happens, and that is the point. Said out loud, the ordinary business of the town starts to sound like a hymn or a litany.


It is all recorded in his spare room.

title: The Picky Eater Project
author: natalieteng74
description:
Are you exhausted by mealtime battles with your picky eater? Do you worry about your child's nutrition, feel guilty about what they eat, or wonder if you're doing something wrong? If picky eating has left you feeling frustrated, anxious, or ashamed, you're in the right place.

Welcome to The Picky Eater Project, the podcast for moms of picky eaters who are ready to let go of mom guilt and shame and find peace around picky eating.

I'm Natalie Teng, MD, a pediatrician, certified life coach, nutrition coach, and mom of three. I help moms navigate the emotional challenges of picky eating so they can feel calmer, more confident, and less overwhelmed at mealtime.

On this podcast, we'll explore picky eating, mealtime battles, mom guilt, shame, nutrition concerns, and the thoughts and expectations that make feeding your child feel so stressful. You'll discover practical strategies, mindset shifts, and coaching tools to help you navigate challenging meals, reduce frustration, and create a more peaceful relationship with food and your child.

Here's the good news: You don't have to change your child's eating habits to start changing how you feel about picky eating. Your child doesn't have to eat more vegetables, try new foods, or clean their plate for you to begin letting go of guilt and shame.

If you're ready to stop second-guessing yourself, step out of the mealtime power struggles, and find more peace—even if your child remains a picky eater—this podcast is for you.

🎧 Subscribe to The Picky Eater Project and start finding peace around picky eating, one meal at a time.

description:
Have you ever wondered if the world has met the real you?
Hosted by Certified Mindshift Life Coach, professional musician and voice teacher Rebekkah Monitz, From Fawn to Free is the ultimate space for high-achieving women who are ready to trade the exhausting performance of people-pleasing for genuine relational freedom.
For decades, Rebekkah lived in a chronic fawn trauma response—perfectly landing every public performance, crossing every "t," and dotting every "i," while running on empty behind closed doors. Now, she is pulling back the curtain on "fawn fatigue," perfectionism, and the unspoken hangover of over-appeasing.
Blending raw, unpolished storytelling with powerful mindshift coaching frameworks, this podcast is a warm, honest guide to resetting your nervous system, understanding your inner system through tools like Internal Family Systems (IFS), and creating real-world evidence of safety. It's time to let your "jazz hands" rest, drop the perfect presentation, and step into the messy, beautiful reality of showing up exactly as you are.

description:
Deep in the forests around Vermont’s Glastenbury Mountain, five people vanished without a trace between 1945 and 1950, giving rise to the "Bennington Triangle" legend. These five high-profile cases—experienced guide Middie Rivers, college student Paula Welden, veteran James Tedford (supposedly from a moving bus), young Paul Jepson, and Frieda Langer (the only victim whose body was ever found), remain unsolved, fueling speculation about everything from serial killers to the supernatural.

In this series, Crawlspace Media's Tim Pilleri and Lance Reenstierna speak with Worcester State University archives librarian Ross Griffiths to break down each individual case and come to the most likely conclusion. In the final episode, Tim, Lance, and Ross speak with Joseph Citro, the author and Vermont folklorist who coined the term "Bennington Triangle".
